Poisson-Lindley-Gamma (Negative Binomial-Lindley) Distribution

NegativeBinomialLindley.Rd

Probability mass, cumulative distribution, quantiles, and random generation for the mean-parameterized Poisson-Lindley-Gamma (PLG), also called the negative binomial-Lindley (NB-L), distribution. The PMF uses a guarded GSL Tricomi-U evaluation with adaptive quadrature as a fallback.

Usage

dplindGamma(
  x,
  mean = 1,
  theta = 1,
  alpha = 1,
  log = FALSE,
  rel.tol = 1e-08,
  subdivisions = 200L,
  method = c("auto", "quadrature")
)

pplindGamma(
  q,
  mean = 1,
  theta = 1,
  alpha = 1,
  lower.tail = TRUE,
  log.p = FALSE,
  rel.tol = 1e-08,
  subdivisions = 200L
)

qplindGamma(p, mean = 1, theta = 1, alpha = 1)

rplindGamma(n, mean = 1, theta = 1, alpha = 1)

Arguments

x

Numeric vector of counts. Negative, infinite, or noninteger counts have probability zero; noninteger counts produce a warning.

mean

Marginal mean \(\mu\), finite and nonnegative. May be a vector for the density, CDF, and quantile functions; must be scalar for random generation. A zero mean gives a point mass at zero.

theta

Lindley parameter, finite and strictly positive. May be a vector except for random generation.

alpha

Gamma dispersion, finite and nonnegative. For positive alpha, the mean-one gamma factor has shape and rate \(1/\alpha\), and variance \(\alpha\). Zero selects the exact Poisson-Lindley limit. May be a vector except for random generation.

log

Logical; return log probabilities from dplindGamma.

rel.tol

Relative tolerance, a scalar between 1e-12 and 1e-3; default 1e-8. Controls adaptive quadrature and, for the PMF, screening of GSL error estimates and log-formula roundoff. It is a numerical target, not a certified bound on the final error.

subdivisions

Maximum number of subintervals for each side of each component integral; an integer of at least 50, default 200.

method

PMF evaluation method. "auto" (default) attempts GSL outside the guarded regions and uses quadrature if any check fails. "quadrature" always uses adaptive quadrature and is useful for validation. There is deliberately no option to force an unchecked GSL value. This argument applies only to dplindGamma.

q

Numeric vector of quantiles. Finite values are rounded down.

lower.tail

Logical; if TRUE, return \(P(Y\le q)\); otherwise return \(P(Y>q)\).

log.p

Logical; return log probabilities from pplindGamma.

p

Numeric vector of probabilities in \([0,1]\).

n

Number of observations to generate: a nonnegative integer scalar.

Value

dplindGamma returns probability masses or log masses; pplindGamma returns cumulative or survival probabilities, possibly on the log scale; qplindGamma returns quantiles; and rplindGamma returns n random counts.

Details

Parameterization and probability mass. Let \(L\) have Lindley density $$f_L(l)=\frac{\theta^2}{1+\theta}(1+l)e^{-\theta l},\quad l>0,$$ and let \(W=L/E(L)\), where \(E(L)=(\theta+2)/[\theta(\theta+1)]\). Conditional on \(W\), \(Y\) is negative binomial with size \(1/\alpha\) and mean \(\mu W\). Equivalently, \(Y\mid W,G\) is Poisson with mean \(\mu WG\), with independent \(G\sim\mathrm{Gamma}(1/\alpha,1/\alpha)\), using the shape-rate parameterization. Thus mean is the marginal mean, not the unnormalized Lindley scale.

The compound probability mass function (PMF) for the Poisson-Lindley-Gamma distribution is $$ f(x\mid\mu,\theta,\alpha)= \frac{ (\theta+2)^2\Gamma(x+1/\alpha) }{ \alpha\mu^2(\theta+1)^3\Gamma(1/\alpha) } \left( \frac{\mu\theta(\theta+1)}{\theta+2} U\left( x+1,2-1/\alpha,\frac{\theta+2}{\alpha\mu(\theta+1)} \right) +\frac{x+1}{\alpha} U\left( x+2,3-1/\alpha,\frac{\theta+2}{\alpha\mu(\theta+1)} \right) \right). $$ This expression applies for \(\mu>0\), \(\theta>0\), \(\alpha>0\), and nonnegative integer \(x\). Here \(U\) is Tricomi's confluent hypergeometric function of the second kind, with positive-integrand representation $$U(a,b,z)=\frac{1}{\Gamma(a)}\int_0^\infty e^{-zt}t^{a-1}(1+t)^{b-a-1}\,dt,\quad a>0,\ z>0.$$ This integral exists for every real \(b\); integer or nonpositive \(b\) is not, by itself, a mathematical singularity of \(U\). The expected value of the distribution is $$E[x]=\mu.$$ The variance is $$\sigma^2=\mu+\left((1+\alpha) \left(2-\frac{2}{(\theta+2)^2}\right)-1\right)\mu^2.$$

GSL instability and automatic fallback. In the PMF above, both Tricomi terms have third argument $$z=\frac{\theta+2}{\alpha\mu(\theta+1)}.$$ The ROOT discussion cited below reports GSL series-convergence failures for \(U(a,b,z)\) when \(a>8\) and \(z\) is close to zero; an example is \(U(9.50606,0.5,0.000160903)\). The final correction in that thread says \(a>8\), superseding the earlier statement \(a<10\). These are historical implementation failures, not singularities of the function. The discussion also concerns Kummer's first-kind function at negative arguments; those examples are not the basis of this PMF's guard, since its Tricomi argument \(z\) is positive.

Additional checks against positive-integrand quadrature with GSL 2.7.1 found underestimated error for large negative second arguments, e.g. x = 0, mean = 1000, theta = 1, alpha = 0.001 (\(1/\alpha=1000\), \(z=1.5\)), where the relative PMF discrepancy was about \(4\times10^{-8}\) despite successful GSL status. The guard \(0<\alpha<0.01\) conservatively excludes this large-negative-b regime; it too is an implementation policy, not a mathematical boundary.

In method = "auto", both U calls are bypassed whenever either first argument exceeds 8 and \(z<1\). Here the first arguments are \(x+1\) and \(x+2\), so this guard applies to \(x\ge7\). The cutoff 1 is a conservative implementation choice around the reported small-positive-argument failures, not a published universal boundary. Tests with GSL 2.7.1 also found inaccurate, successful-status results outside \(z<0.01\) (including \(z\) near 0.12), motivating the wider \(z<1\) guard. Behavior depends on the linked GSL version and on all three arguments. For numerical and computational safeguards, quadrature is also used directly when \(0<\alpha<0.01\), either first argument exceeds \(10^4\), or \(z\) cannot be represented as a positive normal double.

Otherwise, the two U terms are evaluated together with gsl::hyperg_U(..., give = TRUE, strict = TRUE). The complete PMF is recomputed by quadrature if GSL throws an error or warning; returns NULL, missing/malformed fields, NA, NaN, or infinite values; reports nonzero status; returns a nonpositive or subnormal U value; or supplies an invalid error estimate. Each estimated relative U error must be at most rel.tol / 4. A conservative estimate of roundoff in the log formula must also be at most rel.tol / 4. Invalid component probabilities or a final probability outside \((0,1]\) trigger the same fallback. GSL errors are not exposed as warnings when quadrature subsequently succeeds. An unavailable GSL namespace also causes fallback when this file is sourced independently.

Gamma ratios, powers, and the sum of the two positive terms are evaluated on the log scale. A zero U result is treated as possible underflow, never as proof of a zero probability. Neither success status nor an error estimate proves accuracy for every argument. Use method = "quadrature" for independent checks in the parameter range of an application, especially after changing the linked GSL version.

Adaptive quadrature and cumulative probabilities. Write \(X=\theta L\). With probability \(\theta/(1+\theta)\), \(X\sim\mathrm{Gamma}(1,1)\); otherwise, \(X\sim\mathrm{Gamma}(2,1)\). With \(c=(\theta+2)/(\theta+1)\), \(W=X/c\). Quadrature integrates the conditional NB PMF separately against these two positive gamma densities. Each integral uses \(t=\log X\), is scaled at its mode, and is integrated on both sides of the mode with separate width scales. Component probabilities are combined using log-sum-exp. The fallback does not use a difference of hypergeometric functions, truncate the count support, or substitute an arbitrary positive probability floor.

pplindGamma always uses quadrature of the conditional NB CDF or survival function. Upper tails are integrated directly; probabilities near one are obtained from the opposite small tail. At alpha = 0, the conditional routines are Poisson and GSL is bypassed. Small positive alpha is never silently replaced by zero. If quadrature itself fails, the affected result is NaN with a warning; extreme inputs need not be resolvable in double precision. On the ordinary probability scale, sufficiently small probabilities can still underflow to zero; use log = TRUE or log.p = TRUE for such tails.

qplindGamma uses sequential inversion of pplindGamma with its default integration controls, returning the smallest nonnegative integer with CDF at least p. The endpoints are zero for p = 0 and infinity for p = 1 when mean > 0; for mean = 0, every valid quantile is zero. rplindGamma retains inverse-CDF generation using uniform draws and this quantile function. Quantiles and simulation therefore do not benefit from the GSL PMF path and can be slow for large means or probabilities near one.

Numeric arguments of dplindGamma and pplindGamma are recycled to their maximum length; any zero-length numeric argument produces numeric(0). Their logical flags and numerical controls must be scalar. Missing values propagate. Invalid distribution parameters produce NaN with a warning. The quantile function uses Vectorize recycling and simplification; random generation requires scalar parameters. Names on x or q are retained when their length equals the output length.

References

ROOT Forum, Problem in Hypergeometric functions with GSL, including the April 19, 2010 correction and October 3, 2014 follow-up: https://root-forum.cern.ch/t/problem-in-hypergeometric-functions-with-gsl/9507.

GNU Scientific Library Reference Manual, Hypergeometric Functions: https://www.gnu.org/software/gsl/doc/html/specfunc.html.

See also

hyperg_U, integrate, dnbinom

Examples

dplindGamma(0:5, mean = 0.75, theta = 7, alpha = 2)
#> [1] 0.69879293 0.15001417 0.06221417 0.03203763 0.01849751 0.01148442

# Compare the hybrid evaluator with the quadrature reference.
x <- 0:10
fast <- dplindGamma(x, mean = 2, theta = 1, alpha = 0.5)
reference <- dplindGamma(x, mean = 2, theta = 1, alpha = 0.5,
                        method = "quadrature")
max(abs(fast - reference))
#> [1] 6.27276e-15

# x >= 7 and z = (theta+2)/(alpha*mean*(theta+1)) < 1:
# the small-z guard sends this PMF directly to quadrature.
dplindGamma(8, mean = 1e4, theta = 1, alpha = 2/3, log = TRUE)
#> [1] -8.444742

# Log probabilities remain useful when ordinary probabilities underflow.
dplindGamma(10000, mean = 0.1, theta = 1, alpha = 0.5, log = TRUE)
#> [1] -1067.923
pplindGamma(10, mean = 0.75, theta = 3, alpha = 0.5,
            lower.tail = FALSE, log.p = TRUE)
#> [1] -6.722337
dplindGamma(0:3, mean = 0.75, theta = 2, alpha = 0)
#> [1] 0.56320000 0.25190400 0.10838016 0.04538696
qplindGamma(c(0, 0.5, 0.9, 1), mean = 1.67, theta = 0.5, alpha = 0.5)
#> [1]   0   1   4 Inf
rplindGamma(5, mean = 0.5, theta = 0.5, alpha = 2)
#> [1] 0 2 2 0 0
